author: claude
summary: Owner-requested: the recording quality check's clipping detection blocked Keep entirely, with no way to save a clipped take even intentionally. Clipping is now a dismissible warning (icon + message) that leaves Keep enabled; duration-too-short and silence remain hard blocks since those takes are genuinely unusable.

files.change: The clipping branch of checkSampleQuality() now returns ok: true (with hasClipping: true and a warning message) instead of ok: false. Duration and silence checks are unchanged hard blocks.

The captured-state verdict line now renders an AlertTriangle icon + the clipping message when hasClipping && ok, styled via a new --warning modifier class, instead of always collapsing to 'Quality check passed.' when ok is true. Keep's disabled={!verdict?.ok} already falls out correctly now that clipping no longer sets ok: false.

installMediaRecorderMocks() gained an optional decodedBuffer override (plus an exported makeToneBuffer(amplitude) helper) so tests can request a clipping take instead of the default non-clipping tone.

flow_impact: Recording a loud take and clicking Keep now succeeds (with a visible warning) instead of being silently unkeepable.
